newsitem.title: JAPAN: POLL - Japan June M2+CDs growth seen at 2.8-3.1%.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Japan June M2+CDs growth seen at 2.8-3.1%.

text.p: Japan's money supply growth in June is likely to have changed little from May, as bank lending remained sluggish and no significant shifts of funds were detected, economists polled by Reuters said on Monday.
The economists' year-on-year growth forecasts for Japan's broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (CDs) range from 2.8 percent to 3.1 percent.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) will release the data on Thursday at 8.50 a.m. (2350 GMT Wednesday). In May, M2 plus CDs grew a preliminary 3.0 percent from a year earlier.
Mamoru Yamasaki, a senior economist at Paribas Capital Markets in Tokyo, predicted the year-on-year growth rate would be unchanged from the previous month at 3.0 percent.

"There was no major change in the money growth trend. Lending remained sluggish but there were no signs suggesting it might slow even further. On the supply side, no significant shifts of funds took place," Yamasaki said.
DKB Research said in a report that a year-on-year decrease in the government's net payments to the private sector in June was also likely to cap money supply growth.

Paribas's Yamasaki said he expects M2 plus CDs to continue a year-on-year growth rate of around three percent in the coming months, unless a drastic shift of funds takes place or a sharp acceleration or deceleration occurs in bank lending growth.
